# Problem 1


```{r}
birthday_sim = function(group_size) {
  birthdays = sample(1:365, size = group_size, replace = TRUE)
  any(duplicated(birthdays))
}
```

```{r}
birthday_results = tibble(
  group_size = 2:50
) |>
  mutate(
    simulations = map(
      group_size,
      ~ replicate(10000, birthday_sim(.x))
    ),
    probability = map_dbl(simulations, mean)
  )

birthday_results
```

```{r}
birthday_results |>
  ggplot(aes(x = group_size, y = probability)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format()) +
  labs(
    x = "Group Size",
    y = "Probability of a Shared Birthday",
    title = "Probability of a Shared Birthday by Group Size"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

The probability that at least two people share a birthday increases rapidly as group size increases. The simulated probability is approximately 50% when the group size is around 23 people and continues to rise toward 100% as the group becomes larger. This illustrates the birthday paradox: a shared birthday becomes likely even in a group that is much smaller than 365 people.
